hypothesis: Two trace-visible parent failures cost information and answer quality. (1) On the 'who sends these letters/calls' puzzles the 7B spends many questions on what the character feels, believes or suspects (parent i82: 8, i93: 9), which the story does not record: the referee replies Unknown (i93: 14 Unknown) or with an uninformative Yes. (2) The final answer copies questions the referee answered No back in as true (parent i20, i52, i94). If a mental-state question is re-asked once with a note to ask a yes/no question about what happened, and a final answer that reuses most of the distinctive words of a No-answered question is sent back with those questions and an instruction to delete only that claim, then mental-state questions sent drop to about 0, Unknown replies fall on those puzzles, and final answers stop restating No-answered claims. Puzzles where neither trigger fires play exactly as in the parent. The prediction fails if mental-state questions keep being sent, if the re-ask causes not-a-question replies, or if the revision adds new false claims or rewrites the story.
behavior_changes: Question phase: if the model's question matches a mental-state pattern (feel/felt, suspect, believe, think/thought, consider, wonder, aware, theory), the model is re-asked once in the same chat, with a note that the story records what happened and not feelings, and that it should ask one yes/no question about who did what, how or why. The re-asked reply is sent unless it starts with What/Why/How/Who/Where/When/Which (the first version of this change sent two 'What ...?' questions in i90, and the referee rejected both as not a question). In that case the model's original question is sent. Only the accepted question goes into the chat history.

Final answer: after the parent's recap and final prompt produce a draft, the harness flags No-answered questions that share at least 3 content words with the draft, covering at least 60% of the question's content words not in the puzzle text. If any are flagged, the model sees them and is asked to delete only the words that state them, add nothing new and not mention what is false, or else to repeat its answer unchanged. The model's reply replaces the draft, and the draft is kept if the reply is empty. The first wording ('rewrite without that claim') made i94 swap one No-answered claim for another and made i82/i93 append negation sentences, so it was narrowed to deletion only.
preserved_behaviors: Official AR-Bench system prompt, 'Turn t' prompts, full chat with raw referee replies, and AR-Bench's final prompt verbatim.
Parent's stall nudge (no Yes in the last 4 replies) and parent's Yes/No recap before the final prompt, unchanged.
The model writes every question and the final answer. Questions go to the referee unedited, all 25 are used, temperature and max_tokens are unchanged.
When neither trigger fires, the episode is identical to the parent's: i16, i36, i5 and i72 reproduced the parent's questions and final answers exactly (26 calls).

Final run: 10/10 status=ok, parsed_final_answer=True, 25 questions each, not_a_question 0% on all puzzles (the first version had 8% on i90), repeat 0% except i94 at 4%, 26-34 calls per episode. audit.py --task sp: OK.

Mental-state questions sent, parent -> candidate: i82 8->0, i93 9->0, i90 2->0, i52 2->1, i20 1->0, i94 1->0. Unknown replies: i93 14->6, i94 6->5, i82 3->3. Re-asks turned them into questions about what happened, e.g. i93 'Does Emma suspect clairvoyance?' -> 'Are the events unable to occur due to logical inconsistencies?', then a run of Yes about the sender protecting Emma and having the means to prevent the events. i90 'Does Sarah feel anxious?' -> 'Do the calls cause Sarah to take actions?' (Yes).

Mean reply rates, final run vs parent: yes 29.2% vs 32.0%, no 48.4% vs 45.2%, unknown 21.6% vs 22.0%, not_a_question 0% vs 0%. The Yes rate dropped mostly on i52 (0 Yes vs 9), where the run diverged at Q8 and then drifted through 'Was Tom's hometown in a region that ...' questions that got Unknown. The re-ask only touched Q8 there, and the stall nudge did not move the model off that line.

Final-answer revision fired 4 times in the final run. i52 reworded the 'mix-up with a similar-looking person' claim but kept it (not fixed). i82 was a false-positive flag and the answer came back unchanged. i93 deleted the 'influence or authority over the situations' clause. i94 deleted only its last clause, which said the letter was retrieved from a hiding place. None added new claims. In the first run the revision correctly removed 'prior knowledge of her routine' from i94. Final answers on the re-ask puzzles got shorter (i82 143->94 words, i93 131->82, i90 160->116), with less restating of every Yes question.
risks: No outcome signal: fewer Unknowns and fewer copied No claims are proxies for character-F1. The changed trajectories on i52/i82/i90/i93/i94 are single seeded samples, so per-puzzle Yes-rate shifts (especially i52) may be sampling variance as much as the mechanism.

The word-overlap detector is crude. It misses paraphrased No claims (i20 'access to identity and mailing address', i36 'surprise celebration') and flags some that are only topically close (i82). The deletion instruction keeps false positives harmless in these traces, but the 7B sometimes ignores it (i52).

The mental-state regex can catch legitimate fact questions (e.g. 'Was Tom aware ...' when awareness is the twist). It costs one extra call per hit (up to +7 calls on i82), and the retry can still be mental or verbose (i52: same question with a '(Rephrased: ...)' tail).
The parent's known risks are unchanged: the stall nudge repeats every turn during long no-Yes runs, and the recap can still produce list-like answers.
